title: Design System: B1G Sportship — Player Inventory

figure.purpose: The 34px headline number in an analyst-register metric panel.

metric.purpose: 28px stat value on the original register.

pageTitle.purpose: 24px page heading on the analyst register.

headline.purpose: 26px page title on the original register.

title.purpose: 19px card-level name, e.g. a person in a review card.

body.purpose: 15px paragraphs, form inputs, and button labels.

label.purpose: 13px section labels, table cells, and analyst-register body copy.

kbd.purpose: 11px keyboard hint chips and chart axis labels — the floor of the scale.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: The system's only shadow — ambient lift for every card, no hierarchy meaning.

motion.name: fade-in
motion.purpose: Shared entrance for arriving at a new step (select, summary).

motion.name: advance-in
motion.purpose: Signature transition reserved for advancing through the triage queue — reads as moving forward, distinct from a generic entrance.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Ember fill with graphite text — never white, per the Ember Contrast Rule.

components.name: Secondary Button (small)
components.description: The analyst register's compact control size — 13px, used for export and paging actions inside panel headers.

components.name: Panel
components.description: The analyst-register container: white on the grey page ground, hairline border, NO shadow. Depth comes from ground-vs-panel contrast, which is what lets panels butt together at 12px gaps.
components.html:
Placing seekers

Seekers are people asking for a group. Capacity is leaders who said they can take someone.

Content sits here.

components.name: Metric Panel
components.description: A 34px figure with its required explanation line. The sentence is part of the component, not decoration — a bare number here invites the wrong read.

components.name: Discipleship Segment Bands
components.description: The five-segment stack: blue = placed, ember = unplaced, grey = never asked. Rendered in pipeline order, never sorted by size. Every warm band is a step of the brand ramp (OKLCH hue 41.8), so the palette is rooted in the brand with blue as its complement.

components.name: View Chip
components.description: A named worklist filter carrying its own live count. Active state is the accent tint — the one place Ember marks a control's state in this register.

components.name: Accent Badge
components.description: Pill badge tied to the accent's meaning — e.g. the triage queue's position counter. Reserved for genuinely accent-meaningful state, not decorative repetition (a list of tied tags uses Neutral instead).

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Date and text fields on the select step. Solid border, Ember focus ring — never a border-color-only focus change.

components.name: View Switch
components.description: The segmented control in a panel header. Two readings that share a table's columns are one component with a switch, never two panels — count/ratio on the sport grids, and the three roster views.
components.css: .ds-switch { display: inline-flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0; padding: 2px; border: 1px solid var(--color-border-strong); border-radius: 7px; background: var(--color-surface); } .ds-switch-opt { appearance: none; border: 0; background: transparent; padding: 4px 8px; border-radius: 5px; font: 500 12px/1 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; color: var(--color-ink-secondary); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-switch-opt:hover { color: var(--color-ink); } .ds-switch-opt:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent); outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-switch-on, .ds-switch-on:hover { background: var(--color-surface-subtle); color: var(--color-ink); }

components.name: Butterfly Row
components.description: One row of a mirrored comparison: leaders' offer left, seekers' want right, on a shared percentage axis. Both wings are a share of their own population — the populations differ better than two to one, so a shared count axis would read proportional agreement as a shortfall. The printed figure is the share, matching what the bar encodes.

components.name: Capacity Fill Bar
components.description: Seekers against leaders with room, one bar per gender. The whole bar is the supply, the filled part is the demand, and the unfilled remainder is the finding — capacity is not the constraint. Each bar is its own denominator because groups are not mixed, so the two markets never share a scale. Replaced a dumbbell (2026-08-14) that asked the reader to decode a distance.

narrative.overview:
This is an operator's panel, not a showcase — a single admin, alone, weekly, dropping a file and trusting the system to place the obvious cases silently while surfacing only what genuinely needs a human call. Every device in the system serves that: a white canvas with almost no chrome, one accent color spent only where a decision or a status actually lives, generous whitespace that reads as calm rather than empty, and a triage step built to be operated — keyboard shortcuts, a forward-advancing transition, a queue that shrinks as you work it.

The system fuses three references named directly in the brief: Apple Health's native chrome, generous whitespace, and card-based data presentation; Linear's snappy, deliberate, keyboard-fast interaction texture; and Notion/Things 3's calm, content-first, single-item focus. Nothing here is warm or ministry-themed by design — this tool serves a church sports program, but its register is neutral efficient utility, deliberately separated from the program's own identity. It explicitly rejects the generic SaaS admin dashboard: no sidebar, no data-table-plus-chart-widgets scaffold, no decorative navigation chrome standing between the admin and the task. The one exception, added once a real multi-page product existed: a single thin top bar for wayfinding — see Layout and Components → Navigation.
keyCharacteristics: White/clean ground as the overwhelming majority of every screen; color is earned, never ambient.
One accent (`Ember`, #FF6F2F) spent only on primary actions and states that need attention — never decorative, never small standalone text.
Cards are the only container, always soft-shadowed, never bordered-and-shadowed at once.
Motion is signature, not scattered: a shared entrance fade for arriving at a step, a distinct forward-slide reserved for advancing through the triage queue.
No kickers, no eyebrows, no uppercase tracked labels anywhere in the system.

rules.name: The Ember Contrast Rule
rules.body: Ember (#FF6F2F) has a measured WCAG contrast of ~2.8:1 against both white and black at small sizes — it fails body-text contrast either way. Ember therefore only ever appears as a fill (paired with Graphite text on top, never white) or as `Ember Ink` (#C2450F, a darkened same-hue derivative that clears 5:1 on white) when the accent needs to be small text or an icon directly on canvas. Never render raw Ember as text.

rules.name: The One-Voice Rule
rules.body: Ember is the only saturated color with a decorative role in the system. Success and Danger are status signals, not palette options — do not reach for them to add visual variety.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No label in the system is uppercase, letter-spaced, or set above a heading as a kicker. Section labels sit at Label size, sentence case, directly adjacent to the content they describe — never floating above it as a category tag.

rules.name: The One-Shadow Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one shadow value. If a new component seems to need a different depth, that is a signal to reconsider the component, not to add a shadow tier.

rules.name: The Panel Header Icon Rule
rules.body: A panel header may carry a 16px icon in `Graphite Secondary`, but **named sections only** — the panels a reader scans between. A panel that repeats does not: the 40+ seeker panels on `/match` are titled with people's names, and a person is not a category. Forty identical icons are texture, not wayfinding. Metric panels take no icon either; their 34px figure is the focal element and an icon beside it competes.

rules.name: The Borrowed Legend Rule
rules.body: A chart whose two sides are segments — leaders against seekers, in a group against not — takes the segment tokens verbatim rather than picking a fresh pair. The supply/demand butterflies wear seg-leaders on the offer wing and seg-seekers — the brand itself — on the want wing, so a reader who learned the funnel reads them without a second legend.

rules.name: The Switch-In-Place Rule
rules.body: When two readings share a table's columns or a grid's axes and differ only in ranking, filter, or normalisation, they are one component with a switch — never two panels. Three panels printing the same table three times is the failure this rule exists to prevent; the roster's returning / no-show / unplaced views are the case that earned it.

dos: Do spend Ember only on fills paired with Graphite text, or as Ember Ink for small text/icons directly on canvas — never raw Ember as text (The Ember Contrast Rule).
Do keep every card at the single Card shadow value and 16px radius, no exceptions (The One-Shadow Rule).
Do set section/field labels in sentence case at Label size, adjacent to their content — never as an uppercase kicker above it (The No-Eyebrow Rule).
Do use tabular figures only for aligned columns and compact inline counters (queue position, future table columns) — never on a large standalone stat value.
Do reserve Success/Danger strictly for status, never as palette variety.
Do validate any new chart series color with `validate_palette.js` before shipping it — never eyeball CVD-safety.
Do print the figure the mark actually encodes: a share bar gets a percentage beside it and its raw count in the row's title.
Do measure a chart's min-width floor at 390px before trusting its overflow-x-auto wrapper to contain it.
Do open a facetted grid with its Total facet, then run the categories alphabetically, so two grids of the same five things can be read against each other position by position.
donts: Don't introduce a sidebar, or any chrome beyond the one documented top bar — no secondary toolbars, breadcrumbs, or decorative header content.
Don't add a second accent color. One accent, spent deliberately, is the system's discipline.
Don't invent a new chart series hue past the documented palette order — the next slot is aqua, not a generated color.
Don't use white text on Ember; it fails contrast at this hue (~2.8:1) regardless of weight or size.
Don't reach for progress bars, completion badges, or celebratory motion — this is a chore tool, not a gamified habit app.

Don't stack a border, a shadow, and a background-color shift on the same card edge; borders and the one shadow work together, a background shift never joins them (surface and canvas share the same white).
Don't build a second panel for a reading that shares another's columns and differs only in ranking, filter, or normalisation — that is one component with a switch.
Don't give a chart a second colour pair for a distinction the segment palette already carries.
